petition_no: I.A. Diary No. 241/2026 In Diary No. 233/2026
summary: **Parties Present:** Ms. Swapna Seshadri, Advocate, EPTCL Shri Amal Nair, Advocate, EPTCL Shri Devyani Prasad, Advocate, EPTCL 2. The Petitioner, AMNS Power Transmission Company Limited, has filed the Petition (Diary No. 233/2026) for truing up of the transmission tariff for (a) Stage-1 Assets and (b) LILO in accordance with the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2014 (“2014 Tariff Regulations”) for the period from 1.4.2014 to 31.3.2019 and as per the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2019 (“2019 Tariff Regulations”) for the period from - _b) In the alternative, grant deferment of payment of filing fees in respect of the accompanying Petition;_ - _c) Pass any such other of further order as this Commission may deem it and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case.”_ 4. The Petitioner, in support of the reliefs sought in the IA, has submitted as under: 5. The IA was listed for the hearing on 25.5.2026, and after hearing the learned counsel(s) for the Petitioner, the Commission reserved the order on the IA. 6. We have considered the submission of the learned counsel(s) for the Petitioner and perused the documents available on record. The issue arising for consideration in the IA is whether the Petitioner has established sufficient grounds under Regulations 26 and 27 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023 for seeking exemption/ deferment and/or waiver of filing fees? _3) An interlocutory application shall be filed to seek any of the following reliefs:_ _4) In case waiver of payment of fees is sought in respect of any petition, the concerned party shall separately make a request indicating the reasons for such waiver, along with documentary proof, if any, and upload the request for waiver alongwith the petition on the e-filing portal of the Commission.”_ 8. Regulations 26 and 27 of the 2023 COB Regulations permit the filing of an IA seeking procedural reliefs, including exemption/waiver from payment of filing fees, subject to sufficient reasons and supporting material being placed on record. The Petitioner has primarily relied on liquidity constraints, pending tariff recoveries, and financial stress arising out of regulatory and operational factors. However, the Petitioner has not placed on record any audited financial statements, cash flow records, insolvency-related proceedings, or any other documentary material substantiating genuine financial incapacity or exceptional circumstances warranting exemption/ deferment and/or waiver from payment of the prescribed filing fees. 9. We further examined that the financial constraints pleaded by the Petitioner, including pending tariff recoveries, liquidity constraints, and working capital stress, arose out of commercial and regulatory operations undertaken in the ordinary course of its business as a transmission licensee. It is noted that the grounds projected by the Petitioner are not sufficient for a relaxation from compliance with the statutory requirement relating to the payment of filing fees. Any exemption/ deferment and/or waiver from 10. It is noted that the Petitioner, being a commercial entity, cannot ordinarily seek exemption/deferment and/or waiver from compliance with the statutory requirement relating to payment of filing fees, particularly in the absence of adequate material establishing genuine financial incapacity or other exceptional circumstances. 11. Order XXXIII of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908 (CPC), with regard to the institution of suits by indigent persons, provides as under: _“1._ **_ Suits may be instituted by indigent persons _** _-Subject to the following provisions, any suit may be instituted by an indigent person._ _(a) If he is not possessed of sufficient means (other than property exempt from attachment in execution of a decree and the subject-matter of the suit) to enable him to pay the fee prescribed by law for the plaint in such suit, or_ _Explanation II - Any property which is acquired by a person after the presentation of his application for permission to sue as an indigent person, and before the decision of the application, shall be taken into account in considering the question whether or not the applicant is an indigent person._ _Explanation III - Where the plaintiff sues in a representative capacity, the question whether he is an indigent person shall be determined with reference to the means possessed by him in such capacity._ 12. In terms of the explicit provisions under Order XXXIII of CPC, 1908, read with Regulations 26 and 27 of the 2023 COB Regulations, we are of the view that the Petitioner has failed to establish exceptional circumstances warranting the exercise of discretion 13. The Petitioner is directed to rectify all deficiencies notified by the Registry in the main Petition on the e-filing portal within the stipulated time and deposit the filing fee in accordance with the Payment of Fees Regulations. 14. The Registry is directed to register the main Petition (Diary No. 233/2026) only upon compliance with the above directions by the Petitioner. 15. Accordingly, I.A. (Diary) No. 241/2026 stands disposed of in terms of the above discussions and findings.
title: Interlocutory Application under Regulation 26 read with Regulation 27 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023 seeking exemption/ deferment from payment of filing fees. Essar Power Transmission Company Limited
